paper.core_task: Investigating gating mechanisms in softmax attention for transformers

contributions.name: Systematic investigation of gating positions and variants in softmax attention
contributions.author_claim_text: In this work, we investigate gating mechanisms in the standard softmax attention.
contributions.description: The paper systematically explores gating at five distinct positions within the attention layer, testing variants like elementwise/headwise, head-specific/shared, and multiplicative/additive forms.

contributions.name: Analysis of non-linearity and sparsity from gating in attention
contributions.author_claim_text: We identify two factors contributing to the efficacy of gating: (i) Non-Linearity... (ii) Sparsity.
contributions.description: The analysis reveals that gating introduces non-linearity between the value and output projections, enhancing expressiveness, and creates input-dependent sparsity that filters irrelevant information.

contributions.name: Demonstration of attention-sink elimination via sparse gating
contributions.author_claim_text: Sparse gating eliminates the massive activation and attention sink: the initial tokens have large activation values... and disproportionately dominate attention scores.
contributions.description: Empirical verification shows that input-dependent sparse gating after SDPA output eliminates attention sinks and massive activations in both dense and MoE models.
